grh_211c523aef4a6e7b82b9.title: Champion
paragraphs: Midge Kelly is a poor, angry drifter who discovers that boxing may be his way out of a life in which he feels like a nobody. Trainer Tommy Haley sees talent in him and helps turn him into a contender, but success feeds Midgeâ€™s ambition faster than his character. He discards people when they no longer serve him, threatens former lover Grace, abandons loyal relationships and even refuses to leave training when his dying mother calls for him. By the time he reaches the championship, his brother Connie sees how thoroughly the fight business and Midgeâ€™s hunger for status have corrupted him. In a savage title defense against Johnny Dunne, Midge is beaten nearly senseless but refuses to let Tommy throw in the towel. He rallies, knocks Dunne out and hears the crowd finally cheering his name, only to collapse moments later and die. Connie bitterly gives the reporters the conventional line that Midge went out like a champion, even though the victory has cost him everything.

grh_21a8602451f84392dcf2.title: Scandal In The Fourth Dimension
paragraphs: Professor John Boswell refuses to approve his daughter Betty's marriage to young Alec Dale because Alec intends to become an inventor after leaving the Army. Rather than argue directly, Dr. Christian tells Boswell an outrageous college story about Professor Erasmus Doke, his brilliant student Aloysius O'Flannigan and Doke's daughter Patsy. In Christian's tale, Doke's experiments with the fourth dimension leave him only partly visible. Aloysius understands the mathematics well enough to restore him, but will help only if Doke accepts his courtship of Patsy. Doke stubbornly refuses and tries to live half-invisible, producing classroom chaos, public panic and an absurd arrest in which police struggle with the visible and invisible halves of him. Humiliated, Doke finally gives in, Aloysius restores him, and the young couple's engagement follows. Boswell suspects Christian invented the whole story, but the lesson works: he admits he may have been too hard on Alec and agrees to reconsider rather than trying to stop the younger generation from choosing for itself.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_2155558faa503bbc3d7d.title: The Wrath of ZEUS
paragraphs: In 2057, the Zeus 5 computer controls the world's weather and has transformed deserts, agriculture and daily life. When unscheduled rain causes a deadly Los Angeles flood and huge typhoons threaten Japan, officials initially fear that the system itself has begun to malfunction. Their investigation instead shows that the computer has been deliberately given destructive instructions. Technician John Campbell finally admits that he manipulated Zeus because he believed its power should be used boldly and that he was capable of ruling through it. He is arrested, but the crisis leaves the World Council with a harder problem: shutting Zeus down is no longer practical because civilization has been rebuilt around the weather system and has become dependent upon it.

grh_214e476f2274eda8a7a2.title: The Indiscretion of Mr. Edwards
paragraphs: During a circus engagement, Watson poses as the wealthy Sir William Nigel while another distinguished visitor travels incognito as Mr. Edwards. When performer Giselle Gironde is strangled in her dressing room, Edwards and Watson are arrested because the door was watched and no one seems able to have entered. A threatening note from tightrope walker Yvette proves a false lead. Holmes realizes the open window and thin cord make entry unnecessary: jealous animal trainer Pierre stood outside beyond the unmarked snow, lured Giselle to lean out, snapped his long training whip around her neck and cut the lash after strangling her. The matching whip stock and severed lash clear Holmes's companions.

grh_2150e0b59ce934f0517a.title: Melody Ranch - Heart as Big as Texas 50.09.
paragraphs: Gene opens with 'Heart as Big as Texas' before taking responsibility for a troubled youth named Mike who otherwise faces reform school. Gene gives him work, a room and increasing trust, and after weeks of resistance Mike begins to respond. Gene then deliberately entrusts him with $50 as a test. Mike runs away, buys a railroad ticket toward Capital City, but changes his mind at Silver Springs and walks back to the ranch with the unused money. Gene tells him that returning was the proof he needed and closes the story by invoking Kipling's 'If' as a lesson in becoming a man.
This recording comes from [[show|melody-ranch|Melody Ranch]].
Gene Autry western musical-variety series combining songs, comedy and a dramatic Western segment.
